segments.text: with the newly introduced wire bonding
tool in Altium we can now Define
connections directly to die chips
significantly expanding our design
possibilities today I'll walk you
through step by step on how to use this
tool Define die chips and cover all
other features of this tool let's start
by creating a library for the 32bit
controller shown on the screen the
process for defining the symbol is
identical to that of standard components
we Define all the pins and their
parameters which can be imported using a
prepared Excel table through the smart
paste feature into the symbol wizard
after adjusting the pin Arrangement the
symbol might look like this now let's
move on to a more interesting part
creating the footprint for the die chip
in the PCB Library we import the
technical drawing with dimensions for
both the die chip and die pins and then
we need to add two newly introduced
component layer pairs die for the die
chip and die
pins and wire bonding for the
connections between the PCB and the die
next on the top die layer we Define the
die chip using the place extruded 3D
body function according to the
guidelines from the technical drawing
the height must also be set correctly so
that the die pins are positioned
accurately here's how it looks in 3D
now still on the top die we Define the
die pins using Place pad if the
technical sketch is well prepared as it
is here this process goes quickly
although it still needs to be done
manually okay now we have all the die
pins and in the 3D view we can see that
they were automatically placed at the
top of the die chip next we'll focus on
arranging the bond fingers which are the
pads on the PCB that will be connected
to the die pins using B wires since
there are quite a few of them in this
component it's helpful to set a spacing
buffer for their placement then I copy
all the die pins to avoid reassigning
their names I change them to the
appropriate layer and set the correct
dimensions and shapes in this case 0.3
by 0.2 with a rounded rectangle shape
with that in place we can start
arranging them at the specified spacing
here tools like align and distribute are
very useful for demonstration purposes
I've laid out the bond fingers in two
rows along one side now let's move on to
routing the bond wires a new primitive
type has been introduced for this
purpose and is available in the place
menu I've set up a custom shortcut B to
speed up the process additionally to
make routing easier it's helpful to
disable all snapping options except pad
center now we can start routing the
connections it's important to ensure
that the connections go from the die pin
to the Bon finger not the other way
around for two rows of bond wires we can
either alternate connections or if there
are two rows of die pins as well connect
the closer D pins to the nearer Bond
fingers it's also worth adding a central
pad for the ground to connect vsss die
pins at any point during the connection
process we can easily preview how the
bonds will look in reality using the
dynamic 3D view where we can also edit
individual wire bonds to slightly
separate the two rows of wire bonds I'll
reduce the loop height for one row as
you can see the separation is better now
as mentioned earlier changes can also be
made in the 3D view by selecting the
wire bonds we can simultaneously change
their parameters and view the 3D
representation we can choose between
ball and wedge Bond types which are
immediately shown in the visualization
as with other parameters to align the
bond wire angle with the bond finger
rotation we can select the wire bonds
and bond
fingers and then use the pad action
command to align the bond finger with
the bond wire as you can see the angles
are instantly corrected which simplifies
the manufacturing process once the PCB
lib is ready we add it to the component
and place it on the schematic after
routing the traces and adding net labels
we move on to the layout as with other
changes on the schematic we import the
updates to the PCB and our die chip
appears in the top right corner of the
board like other components besides
onetoone die to bond finger connections
more complex configurations like die to
die die to copper and Copper to Copper
connections are all Al possible in each
of these cases multiple wire bonds can
be used for instance for power traces
now let's take a look at the rules and
constraints a new rule type has been
added to the routing section allowing us
to Define limits for the basic
parameters of wire bonding this option
is available in both the classic rules
section and the constraint manager if
any rule is not met the affected wire
Bond will be highlighted in Green in
both 2D and 3D
views now let's move on to documentation
in draftsman wire bonds can be displayed
both in the board assembly
View and individually in the component
View
as with other components the appropriate
layers should be
enabled and we can increase the scale
for clearer
documentation another new production
document for wire bonding is the wire
bonding table report available under
assembly output in the out job file
after generating this table we get a CSV
file that can be easily parsed since the
separator is a comma making it highly
readable that's all for today thank you
very much more details and documentation
on wirebonding can be found in altum's
documentation resources

title: Advanced Wire Bonding Techniques in Altium Designer - Demo
